message:
Tree viewport: order-statistic sibling index for row mapping

rowAt, offsetWithinParent (visibleIndexOf, visibleIndexOfCoordinate,
residency ancestors) and the window seek walked the materialized
siblings of each parent linearly, O(k) per level. Each parent now owns
an AVL tree over its materialized children (VirtualTreeSiblingIndex):
nodes are the topology ids, keys are read from the live childIndices
lane (a sibling shift keeps in-order), weights are the visibleExtraRows
lane and are adjusted where refreshVisibleExtra and
propagateVisibleContribution change it. Prefix sums and the row descent
are O(log k) per level; materializedChildId, linkSorted and unlink use
the same tree, so bind is O(log k) instead of O(k).

Test_VirtualTreeOrderStatistic runs seeded random scripts (insert,
materialize, dematerialize, move, expand, collapse, setChildCount,
removeCoordinate, releaseSubtree at random depths; one model with
100,000 materialized siblings) and compares every rowAt,
visibleIndexOf, visibleIndexOfCoordinate, window and residency answer
with the linear walk, kept as a test-only reference.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Tree viewport: measured linear path for small sibling sets, row-mapping benchmark

Queries on a parent whose sibling index is at most 4 high (at most 15
materialized children) walk the sibling chain: one JVM per k, the walk
measured faster up to k = 8 to 12 and the descent faster from k = 16.
rowAt no longer looks up the next sibling; only the window seek does.

VirtualTreeOrderStatisticBenchmark (plain main in the test tree) uses
only API present before and after the index, so the same class measures
the linear walk and the index, plus a Fenwick tree over logical child
indices (the rejected alternative).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
